heading: As SAE dictionaries grow, coarse features split into finer, nearby features
definition: as an SAE's dictionary grows, a coarse feature is replaced by several finer features that together cover its inputs and lie near its direction.
summary: Independent groups see the pattern in Llama-3.1-8B, speaker and astronomy-text embeddings, and small vision and language models, but mostly for hand-picked features; much of the other support shares an author with an original study. Splitting is often partial: larger SAEs also add new features unlike any in smaller ones, and finer features nest only partly under coarse ones across sizes; the only study that measures how well the finer features together match the coarse one counts mismatches both ways and finds only a partial match.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy/theory: mixed. In the wide-limit theory, the narrowest global optimum has one atom per data ray. Extra atoms cannot lower the loss beyond that, but wider solutions, such as one atom per datapoint, are also optimal. Toy runs on few-ray data use 4 of 30 and 2 of 10 neurons (arXiv:2606.02385). lw:jYomRhKiffA6Jnrij is the authors' own summary of the same work, not an independent source. Synthetic ground truth gives rare near-duplicate splits (arXiv:2609.10299, limits_scope). <1B: R2. Evidence comes from GPT-2 small, the 4-layer TinyStories model, the Pythia-160M/CLIP/DINOv2 backbones and the original's one-layer transformer. The GPT-2 small layer-8 posts lw:WsPyunwpXYCM2iN6t, lw:TMAmHh4DdMr4nCSr5 and lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq, and the TinyStories paper arXiv:2503.17547, each share an author with the original arXiv:2502.04878, so they count as R1, not R2. lw:zbebxYCqsryPALh8C carries no shared-author flag but reports the same TinyStories example as arXiv:2503.17547. The R2 at this scale rests on arXiv:2610.23801 (Pythia-160M, GPT-2 Small layer 9, CLIP ViT-B/16, DINOv2-B/14; no shared author), with a weak, figure-only GPT-2 small aggregate from arXiv:2502.17332 (no flag). Counts put most of these studies in size 'not stated' (versions.V1.studies_by_size: not stated 16, <1B 1). 1-10B: R2 on one independent study and one selected feature (versions.V1.studies_by_size 1-10B = 3): a Llama-3.1-8B feature (arXiv:2410.20526, no shared author). The qualitative Gemma-2-2B BatchTopK results (lw:rKM9b6B2LqwSB5ToN) share an author with arXiv:2502.04878 and count as R1. Incomplete nesting in Gemma 2 2B / Qwen3 4B (arXiv:2602.11881, no shared author) is limits_scope. 10-100B and >100B: no study (no counts key).
suggested_status.reason: The original (TITLE:Towards Monosemanticity, one-layer transformer) shows splitting qualitatively. Groups with no shared-author flag reproduce the qualitative pattern on other models and modalities: Llama-3.1-8B (arXiv:2410.20526, with a random-cosine control), Titanet speaker embeddings (arXiv:2502.00127, peer reviewed), astro-ph text embeddings (arXiv:2408.00657), and vision and language backbones under ConSDL (arXiv:2610.23801). The author lists of arXiv:2410.20526 and arXiv:2610.23801 share no name with an original; arXiv:2502.00127 and arXiv:2408.00657 carry no SAME GROUP mark in the studies index. Five V1 studies do share an author with the original arXiv:2502.04878, so they count toward R1, not R2: lw:WsPyunwpXYCM2iN6t (Patrick Leask); lw:TMAmHh4DdMr4nCSr5, lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq and lw:rKM9b6B2LqwSB5ToN (Bart Bussmann); and arXiv:2503.17547 (Bart Bussmann, Neel Nanda; the TinyStories model, ICML). These flags come from the studies index and the author lists; the V1 pack headers carry no shared-author flag. GPT-2 calendar features come from lw:WsPyunwpXYCM2iN6t. There, weekday and month features split qualitatively across layer-8 residual SAEs of 768 to 98304 latents, and year features split only partly, with single-year features mainly in the largest SAEs. The study has no controls and gives no counts for months. Counts: versions.V1.verdicts.supports.studies = 14, limits_scope.studies = 9, challenges.studies = 0; versions.V1.tested_with_controls = 7. Limits: union coverage is not measured as such. The only coverage-type measure, arXiv:2602.11881's Hamming distance between each parent and the logical OR of its children, counts mismatches in both directions, so it cannot separate parent inputs the children miss from child firing outside the parent. Standard ReLU SAEs split in only 12–37% of consistent atoms (arXiv:2610.23801). Larger SAEs add novel and composed latents. In arXiv:2502.04878 (itself an original source per counts.originals), 657 GPT2-1536 latents have low max cosine to GPT2-768, and some reconstruction latents compose several smaller-SAE latents. The stitching post gives about 35% novel features as an aggregate over larger SAEs at the same site, with no size pair named (lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq). Nesting is incomplete at 1-10B (arXiv:2602.11881). Some features recur unsplit (O-type stars, arXiv:2408.00657) or split only partly (calendar years, lw:WsPyunwpXYCM2iN6t). The 'causal intervention' evidence type covers only feature swaps and additions inside SAE reconstructions. Counts: versions.V1.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 5, and these are the five studies named above. So the GPT-2 small layer-8 calendar, meta-SAE and stitching evidence, arXiv:2503.17547's TinyStories example and the Gemma-2-2B first-letter results are the original group's extension. lw:zbebxYCqsryPALh8C, which reports the same TinyStories example, and arXiv:2502.17332's weak GPT-2 small aggregate carry no flag. The R2 therefore rests on arXiv:2410.20526 (one selected feature), arXiv:2610.23801 (its own ConSDL method splits more than the standard SAEs it compares), and arXiv:2502.00127 and arXiv:2408.00657 (selected features in embedding SAEs).
suggested_status.open_questions: Results that would change the level: (a) a one-directional union-coverage measure (the fraction of a coarse latent's activations that its children cover; arXiv:2602.11881's Hamming distance on Gemma 2 2B and Qwen3 4B mixes both mismatch directions) for standard SAEs at three or more sizes on a model of 1B or more, by a group independent of all originals; (b) any test on a model above 10B; (c) whether the low split fractions for standard ReLU/TopK SAEs (arXiv:2610.23801) also hold on LLM residual streams; (d) an independent test, by a group sharing no author with either original, that tracks more than one selected feature across dictionary sizes in a 1-10B LLM or in GPT-2 small layer-8 SAEs. At 1-10B the R2 rests on one Llama-3.1-8B feature (arXiv:2410.20526), and the matched-feature GPT-2 small layer-8 evidence is the original group's (lw:WsPyunwpXYCM2iN6t, lw:TMAmHh4DdMr4nCSr5, lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq). A success would firm up R2 at those scales; a failure would argue for C there. Whether lw:zbebxYCqsryPALh8C is independent of arXiv:2503.17547 is not settled by these records; (e) a study showing that standard SAEs mostly keep coarse features unchanged across sizes would argue for C.

source.authors: Trenton Bricken; Adly Templeton; Joshua Batson; Brian Chen; Adam Jermyn; Tom Conerly; Nicholas L Turner; Cem Anil; Carson Denison; Amanda Askell; Robert Lasenby; Yifan Wu; Shauna Kravec; Nicholas Schiefer; Tim Maxwell; Nicholas Joseph; Alex Tamkin; Karina Nguyen; Brayden McLean; Josiah E Burke; Tristan Hume; Shan Carter; Tom Henighan; Chris Olah

original_result.setup: They compared SAEs of several dictionary sizes, from 512 features upward, trained on a one-layer transformer.
original_result.result: One base64 feature in the 512-feature SAE splits into three in the 4,096-feature SAE (letters, digits, encoded ASCII text), which together seem to fire wherever it did, and similar features have small angles between their decoder vectors. The evidence is qualitative, and features can also merge, so it is not a simple tree.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: In Llama-3.1-8B, finer 32x-wide SAE features lay close in direction to one coarse 8x-SAE harmful-events feature.
A coarse periodicity feature persisted while finer related features appeared in larger SAEs.
A general female-words latent gave way to a specialized Lily latent as SAEs grew.
A Spanish speaker-embedding latent split into male and female latents at 300 latents.
Some GPT-2 Small SAE latents split into two nearby, more specific latents in larger SAEs.
Theory predicts that widening a dictionary refines categories toward one feature per data direction (ray).
Coarse weekday and month features split into single-day and single-month features in larger SAEs.
In BatchTopK SAEs, first-letter features were often split across several latents.
A female-words latent split into Sue and Lily name latents as SAEs grew.
A GPT-2-small 'talk' latent split into seven finer latents, all close in direction.
In GPT-2 small, smaller-SAE features and nearby larger-SAE features formed parent-child families.
Theory says dictionary learning keeps splitting features until each data direction (ray) has its own feature.
In larger GPT-2 small SAEs, features were activated by fewer distinct single tokens (unigrams).
In ConSDL sparse-coding dictionaries, about half of seed-stable coarse features gained two or more finer neighbours.
Some astronomy-text SAE features recurred without splitting, and matches across SAE sizes were often inconsistent.
Some larger-SAE latents matched several smaller latents, showing composition rather than splitting.
Synthetic diffuse-regime SAEs split in a minority of runs, only at the larger dictionary size.
When data lay along few directions (rays), a wider dictionary added no more split features.
GPT-2 calendar-year features did not split cleanly as SAEs grew.
In Matryoshka SAEs, which nest smaller dictionaries in larger ones, first-letter features stayed almost entirely unsplit.
About 35% of larger-SAE features were novel, and finer features did not fully replace coarse ones.
In Gemma 2 and Qwen3 SAEs, coarse features missed part of their finer features' inputs.
Standard ReLU and TopK SAEs split far less often than ConSDL sparse-coding dictionaries.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Union coverage: no study measures what fraction of a coarse feature's activations the union of its finer features covers. The only coverage-type measure is arXiv:2602.11881's Hamming distance between each parent and the logical OR of its children (baseline 30.6–78.9, Table 3; V1.wording_issues[1]). It counts mismatches in both directions, so it cannot separate parent inputs the children miss from child firing outside the parent. Other near measures are reconstruction MSE after swaps (lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq#r13), parent-given-child firing rates, which measure containment rather than coverage (arXiv:2602.11881), and the original's qualitative 'seem to jointly cover' (TITLE:Towards Monosemanticity...#R2).

wording_issues.issue: Coarse features often persist next to the finer ones. In lw:WsPyunwpXYCM2iN6t#r2, 3 all-weekday features remain at 98304 latents alongside 7 single-day features. In arXiv:2408.00657#r3, the top-level periodicity feature persists; in #r5, O-type stars recurs with cosine >0.98 at every size. In arXiv:2610.23801#r6 and #r7, ReLU and TopK retriever atoms stay at cosine 0.99 and 0.98. In arXiv:2503.17547#R5, the parent S/3/66 remains but stops firing on 'Lily', which is a hole rather than a replacement. In lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq#r1, a GPT2-1536 feature matches a GPT2-768 feature at cosine 0.99.

The original states it qualitatively ('seem to jointly cover', R2) and shows it only in figures. arXiv:2602.11881 compares each parent's activation with the logical OR of its children (Hamming distance, counting mismatches in both directions). It does this in independently trained JumpReLU SAEs with post-hoc parent assignment. Baseline distances (Table 3): 34.6 at Gemma 2 2B layer 6; 36.1 / 61.9 / 78.9 at layer 13 for target L0 50 / 80 / 100; 30.6 at layer 20; 46.4 at Qwen3 4B layer 18. The authors' HSAE gives lower distances. Because the distance counts both directions, it does not separate parent inputs the children miss from child firing outside the parent. The same study's P(parent | child), 0.309–0.729, measures only child firing outside the parent (containment), not coverage. In GPT-2 small layer-8 SAEs, swapping smaller-SAE feature structures for their larger-SAE counterparts generally increases MSE and almost always decreases L0 (lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq#r13).

wording_issues.issue: Nearness is usually set by a threshold that also defines the parent-child link, so it holds partly by construction (lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq#r10 verdict; lw:TMAmHh4DdMr4nCSr5#r1 uses >0.7; arXiv:2610.23801#r3 uses ≥0.7). Thresholds differ between studies: 0.7 for GPT-2 and 0.4 for Gemma Scope SAEs in arXiv:2502.04878, and a masked activation cosine of about 0.4 in the original, chosen for readability. One measured value is a farthest pairwise cosine of 0.28 among 36 selected features, against random maxima of 0.09 and 0.10 (arXiv:2410.20526#r2). The original's not-in-rows note says the split base64 features share similar decoder vectors but have encoder vectors tilted apart. The original's R4 uses activation similarity, not decoder geometry.

wording_issues.issue: Cross-size relations are not all one-to-many refinements. Some larger latents combine several smaller ones (arXiv:2502.04878#R7), and about 35% of larger-SAE features are novel (lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq#r12). In a synthetic setting, 'splits' are near-duplicate atoms on one true feature (arXiv:2609.10299#R33). An excerpt from the original's own text says the refinement is 'more complex than a tree'.

wording_issues.issue: Growth alone does not set the outcome. Splitting varies with SAE architecture (ConSDL 45–55% vs ReLU 12–37%, arXiv:2610.23801#r3, #r4) and objective (Matryoshka keeps first-letter features unified, lw:rKM9b6B2LqwSB5ToN#r3). It varies with sparsity: the latent size at which the Spanish feature splits varies with TopK K (arXiv:2502.00127#r5). It also varies with data geometry: with few rays, extra width adds no split atoms (arXiv:2606.02385). Some supporting evidence comes from dictionaries that are not SAEs: ConSDL and idealized vanilla dictionary learning.

wording_issues.phrase: a coarse feature is replaced by several finer features
wording_issues.issue: The statement gives no frequency, and most support is hand-picked single features (talk, weekdays, female words, Spanish, periodicity, one Llama-3.1-8B feature). Where rates are reported, 12–37% of consistent ReLU SAE atoms have ≥2 counterparts at 4×→16× (arXiv:2610.23801#r4). The stitching post's intro says about 65% of larger-SAE features are 'similar' (identical or split). This is an aggregate over larger SAEs at the same site, with no size pair named, and it lumps persistence with splitting (lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq#r12). For the GPT2-1536 vs GPT2-768 pair, 879 of the 1536 GPT2-1536 features have maximum cosine >0.7 to a GPT2-768 feature (#r8).

method_sensitivity.what: On the same four backbones at 4×→16× (cosine ≥0.7), consistent atoms with ≥2 counterparts are 45–55% for ConSDL (arXiv:2610.23801#r3), 12–37% for ReLU SAEs (#r4), and 'substantially lower' for TopK (#r5). On Gemma-2-2B layer 8, first-letter features stay almost entirely unified in a Matryoshka SAE but frequently split in BatchTopK SAEs (lw:rKM9b6B2LqwSB5ToN#r3, #r4). Parent-given-child firing in independent JumpReLU SAEs vs HSAE: 0.651 vs 0.752 (Gemma 2 2B layer 6) and 0.309 vs 0.347 (Qwen3 4B layer 18) (arXiv:2602.11881).

Titanet voice SAEs: the latent dimension at which the Spanish feature splits varies with K, rising up to around 300 latents and then plateauing, per the method line (arXiv:2502.00127#r5). Gemma 2 2B layer 13 independent SAEs: P(activp | activc) is 0.662 at target L0 50, 0.634 at L0 80 and 0.619 at L0 100 (arXiv:2602.11881). Top-k text-embedding SAEs, astro-ph and cs.LG pooled (Fig. 9): nearest-neighbour decoder cosine falls as k and n rise; figure-only, cannot_determine (arXiv:2408.00657#r1, #r2). Recurrence is more common at lower k: over 1100 triplets recur at cosine >0.95 across n=3072, 6144 and 9216 for k=16, dropping sharply as k rises (#r6, Fig. 18a; cannot_determine, since recurrence does not test splitting). Synthetic study: at M=256, γ=0.5, no λ from 10^-4 to 10^-2 gives a split (arXiv:2609.10299#R23–#R27). The only canonical split cell is M=512, γ=0.5, λ=10^-3, 5/20 runs, so it differs from its M=256 twin by M, not λ (#R30).

Parent-child links come from cosine thresholds set by each study: a masked activation cosine of about 0.4 in the original, chosen to keep graphs readable (footnote 32), with the P features found manually; 0.7 for GPT-2 and 0.4 for Gemma Scope SAEs in arXiv:2502.04878; 0.7, called somewhat arbitrary, in lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq. The match path changes results: direct SAE16→SAE64 and chained SAE16→SAE32→SAE64 matches give roughly bimodal overlap (arXiv:2408.00657#r7). Decoder cosine tracks the masked activation metric at R² 0.87 for pairs above 0.5 (not-in-rows lines of lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq and arXiv:2502.04878). The ConSDL advantage persists when ≥3 or ≥5 counterparts are required (arXiv:2610.23801, not in rows).

method_sensitivity.what: GPT2-small SAEs, decoder top-1 matching at τ=0.7, OpenWebText vs TinyStories: 72.77% vs 77.25% of 6,144 latents matched in 12,288; 89.22% vs 78.16% of 3,072 matched in 12,288; 89.25% vs 80.01% of 3,072 matched in 6,144 (lw:ATsvzF77ZsfWzyTak#r7–#r12). The rows are cannot_determine for V1, and the study has no V1 verdict: a top-1 match cannot show a one-to-many split.

Independent-SAE nesting, P(activp | activc) at L0 ≈ 50: Gemma 2 2B layer 6 0.651, layer 13 0.662, layer 20 0.729; Qwen3 4B layer 18 0.309. The verdict calls the Qwen case one where the parent is absent on most child activations (arXiv:2602.11881).

Theory: with data spanning many rays from the optimal bias, widening keeps splitting up to one atom per ray (arXiv:2606.02385#r4; lw:jYomRhKiffA6Jnrij#R1, a post that presents arXiv:2606.02385 as its paper, so not independent). In toy simulations with few rays, extra width adds no split atoms: 4 of 30 and 2 of 10 neurons active (arXiv:2606.02385, from text). Synthetic nested dictionary, M=256, λ=10^-2, 20 seeds: 0 runs with a split at each nesting fraction γ = 0.0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8 and 1.0 (arXiv:2609.10299#R21, #R22, #R27, #R28, #R29, Table 1). In that slice, alignment is indistinguishable for γ≤0.5, with a mild decline at γ≥0.8. In the 165-cell companion grid, 34 cells show splits (#R33), but split counts per γ are not reported for the grid.

Within single studies the outcome differs by feature. In GPT-2 layer-8 residual SAEs, the smallest SAE's single weekday or month feature splits into many specific features. Calendar years show what the post calls a more complex pattern: most year features cover year ranges or decade starts and ends, and more than a few single-year features appear only in the largest SAEs (lw:WsPyunwpXYCM2iN6t#r2, #r4, #r5). Periodicity splits while O-type stars recurs unsplit at cosine >0.98 (arXiv:2408.00657#r3, #r5). In CLIP ViT-B/16, the ConSDL retriever atom splits six ways while the ReLU and TopK retriever atoms persist (arXiv:2610.23801#r1, #r6, #r7). Most support comes from hand-selected features.

status_amendment.public_note: We checked which studies share authors with the original papers: five of them, including the GPT-2 calendar, stitching and meta-SAE posts and the Matryoshka work, are by members of the original group, so they now count as extensions rather than independent reproductions. The level stays R2 because unrelated groups still find splitting in Llama-3.1-8B, small vision and language models, and voice and text embeddings, though in models of 1-10B parameters the independent support is now a single selected feature.
